messages:
sam: alerting — SIEM shows a cluster of SSO anomalies starting ~11:05 UTC: 18 session_revoke events in 12m, impossible-travel flags for 5 distinct users across 3 tenants. seeing MFA push floods for same identities. attaching sample logs below. :rotating_light:

security-bot: automatic detection: sso.anomaly.impossible_travel (score: 0.82) triggered for user_ids: [u_172, u_999, u_420] — correlated with session_revokes and auth.push.failed_count spike.

sam: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-20T11:05:12Z user=u_172 src_ip=34.72.12.9 geo=NL -> US delta=3165km user_agent=Mozilla/5.0 event=session_revoke reason=anomaly
2026-03-20T11:07:03Z user=u_999 src_ip=3.14.88.1 geo=US -> NL delta=3120km user_agent=python-requests/2.31 event=auth.push.failed_count=8
2026-03-20T11:12:47Z user=u_420 src_ip=18.203.45.2 geo=DE -> US delta=4200km event=session_revoke
```

maya: pinging oncall +sec — is this tied to the RBAC cleanup we rolled earlier today? any token-format or KMS changes?

alex: KMS key rotation completed at 09:02 UTC but we did not rotate service-account keys. No config changes to RBAC that touch auth flows. I did notice a short-lived downgrade of token TTL from 24h -> 15m in the deploy log at 09:05 (probing change left behind by canary). Investigating if refresh flows misbehaved.

jordan: looking at IPs now — many hops between eu-west and us-east inside minutes. not classic VPN; ASNs differ. could be credential replay via distributed proxy. also seeing repeated push attempts from same device fingerprint for some users (fingerprint: ff:12:4b:9a).

sam: containment proposal: revoke active sessions for affected user_ids only, throttle auth.push to 4/min for those tenants, and add a temporary rule to rate-limit session creation from the suspect ASNs. do not do a tenant-wide disable. thoughts?

maya: agree with scoped revokes. add: capture full audit trail for each revoke (KMS envelope id, token id, refresh token id). also check the KMS rotation audit at 09:02 for suspicious access patterns. we need an evidence bundle before customer comms.

alex: running selective revoke now — script: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/admin/sessions/revoke -d '{"user_id":"u_172","scope":"active_tokens","reason":"sso-anomaly-1765551234"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REVOKER_KEY'``` will post results when done.

incident-bot: task created: INC-2026-3345 assigned to alex, due 2026-03-20T13:00Z — action: selective session revocation and result upload to /incidents/INC-2026-3345/evidence.

jordan: alex — results?

alex: done for u_172,u_999,u_420 and three additional users flagged by correlation. revocations accepted, sessions removed within ~6s each. threw one 500 on first attempt (retriable) — final status: success. uploaded revoke logs to incident bundle.

csm-ryan: heads-up — two of the affected users are customer admins for Tenant t-88 and t-47. I'll prepare an incident note for CX and offer guidance. we should avoid alarmist language until we confirm scope.

maya: good. next: we need to tune our auth push policy. temporary mitigation options: increase verification threshold (device attestation + IP velocity), enforce rate-limit on push deliveries, and enable fallback to TOTP for these tenants. which is fastest?

sam: fastest is to throttle push deliveries and flip to require TOTP for affected tenants (config flag). we can ship throttle in 10m, TOTP enforcement in ~30m (depends on UI flow).

jordan: I pushed an auth rule to WAF to rate-limit the suspect ASNs — monitoring for false positives. so far no user complaints.

maya: action items: 1) alex — full audit bundle (revoke logs, KMS access logs, deploy logs) — due EOD. 2) sam/jordan — auth throttle & WAF rule deployed — monitor for reduction in push flood metrics. 3) csm-ryan — customer comms draft in #customer-success for review. 4) security: open post-incident writeup & runbook update for SSO-improbable-travel scenario (assign me).

sam: quick check: could this be a stale deployment that changed token TTL and caused cascade of refreshes hitting auth and causing push storms? alex?

alex: plausible — token refresh churned at 09:05 for many services. I'm pulling service logs to confirm. if so, postmortem should call out deployment gating for auth-config changes and add a canary kill-switch.

security-bot: detection metrics update: auth.push.deliveries per minute peaked at 2400 (baseline 120). impossible_travel alerts reduced to 0 after revokes & throttles. continuing to monitor.

maya: Once we confirm root cause, we need two mitigations for long-term: 1) require audit-logged RBAC changes + explicit approval window for auth-related config, 2) add a KMS-rotation-impact smoke test that simulates token refresh churn. add both to roadmap.

alex: found correlated deploy: deploy-id=deploy-5378 changed auth.token.ttl from 24h to 15m at 09:05 and a rollback at 09:09. several refresh loops observed in logs between 09:05-09:15. looks like the canary left some nodes on the shorter TTL.

maya: that explains it. root cause = partial rollout of token TTL change -> refresh storms -> mass push deliveries -> MFA fatigue + session revokes. Decision: update runbook to require global-config lock during TTL experiments and a quick rollback script.

sam: good outcome. next steps: file postmortem, schedule a 30-min blameless review, and surface RBAC/ops gating. leaving this thread once incident doc created. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
